text:
Tori: FYI ap-southeast-1: seeing repeated CA scale-ups where new spot GPU nodes come up but kube-scheduler refuses our gpu workloads. looks like a driver/label mismatch across spot pool variants.
Maya: ugh, any recent launch template or AMI roll?
Tori: not from our side. node names: gpu-spot-aps1-a-7f9, gpu-spot-aps1-b-3c2. CA logs show 'no nodes available that match node selector' even though nodes report capacity.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up node-group gpu-spot-aps1-auto (desired=3 -> 5) at 2026-08-12T02:11:12Z
Egor: can you paste node labels & nvidia driver info? sounds like some nodes have old driver or different instance-type label.
Tori: paste: ```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-spot-aps1 -o wide
NAME                          STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   NODE-POOL
gpu-spot-aps1-a-7f9           Ready    <none>   1h    v1.28.4   10.4.3.12     gpu-spot-aps1-a
gpu-spot-aps1-b-3c2           Ready    <none>   10m   v1.28.4   10.4.4.21     gpu-spot-aps1-b
```
and node labels excerpt: ```
node.k8s.amazonaws.com/instance-type=g4dn.xlarge
accelerator.nvidia.com/gpu=true
redwood/gpu-driver-version=510.59
```
the newer nodes show redwood/gpu-driver-version=525.60
Maya: scheduler allocates by driver-friendly tolerations? we have pod affinity on driver-version: ">=510"? I thought we relied on device plugin only.
Egor: our device-plugin checks kernel+driver; if driver < pod.min-driver then plugin marks capacity 0. CA sees capacity then scheduling fails — causes thrash (scale up -> pod pending -> scale up again).
Tori: saw this in cluster-autoscaler logs: ``ERROR: pod X: unschedulable, node(s) had 0/1 GPUs available (device-plugin mismatch)``
oncall: quick mitigation: cordon the suspect spot nodes from pool gpu-spot-aps1-b and drain with --ignore-daemonsets so running jobs move to nodes with correct driver.
Maya: we also should prewarm a tiny ondemand pool in the same AZ to absorb traffic while we roll the spot pool AMI. propose gpu-ondemand-aps1-prewarm size=2 ramp=0.
Egor: agree. long-term: patch autoscaler to prefer instance-type affinity across AZs so CA doesn't mix launch-templates with different AMIs in the same logical pool. also add a node-liveness check that reports device-plugin readiness to CA metrics.
Tori: cost tradeoffs: prewarm ~2 nodes $$ estimate ~ $1.2k/mo but reduces tail latency and prevents double-scaling. worth it for customer SLAs.
Maya: plan: (1) cordon+drain bad nodes (Tori, now) (2) create gpu-ondemand-aps1-prewarm (Maya, 30m) (3) patch LT/AMI for spot pool and roll with 20% batch (Egor, today) (4) autoscaler policy change ticket (Egor)
Egor: creating ticket INFRA-1749 for autoscaler affinity + device-plugin metric hook.
Tori: doing cordon/drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-spot-aps1-b-3c2 && kubectl drain gpu-spot-aps1-b-3c2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
infra-bot: deploy-bot: created node-pool gpu-ondemand-aps1-prewarm (min=2,max=4) in ap-southeast-1a
Maya: thanks. after prewarm we'll shift canary workloads back and roll the spot LT. will monitor CA metrics and pod pending histogram. :thumbsup:
oncall: ping me if pods still pending after the drain so I can escalate to cloud support.
Tori: will report back in ~15m once drain completes and we see rescheduling.
